CXC-IC-INTENT.title: The Intelligence Is a Bus Peer — the Ultimate HAL Peripheral

properties.definition: an Intelligence is declared onto the ComposeBus exactly as the HAL declares a peripheral ([CXC-HALD-DECLARE]): a node with an interface KIND (`channel`), a `config` (its bootstrap), a `calibration` (its dusk gifts), and a role (`transactional` — you send it a message, it acts, it emits, it has a lifecycle). It is a co-equal peer among the MCUs, the WLED adaptor, and the bridged hubs — not the control plane over them. Any bus participant reaches it through ordinary namespaces, ignorant that a mind is behind them, the same way it reads `env/temperature` ignorant of whether a DS18B20 or a bridged HA entity is the source.

an Intelligence is declared by a meta-object `{ role_descriptor, soul, dusk_gifts[], channel, lifecycle }`. `role_descriptor` + `soul` are the STABLE identity; `dusk_gifts[]` are the calibration (pointers to the registration-protocol surfaces, not their content); `channel` binds the transport ([CXC-IC-CHANNEL]); `lifecycle` sets the self-direction policy ([CXC-IC-LIFECYCLE]). Declaring an Intelligence is CONFIGURATION, not recoding ([plt.cio:SPEC:DP-CIO-1]) — the same instance, re-pointed at a new soul + gifts, is a new role; define-once, present-many.

the duplex transport is Claude Code CHANNELS (an MCP server that PUSHES `notifications/claude/channel` events into a running session as `<channel source=... >` tags, and — two-way — exposes a `reply` tool the instance calls to send back). It maps directly: inbound events ≙ `compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/in`; the `reply` tool ≙ `compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/out`. The channel's server name addresses it (`server:composeio-channel`); the `<id>` scopes the bus topics and the routing `meta`.
properties.instantiation: a session joins by registering the channel MCP server and launching with BOTH `--channels server:composeio-channel` AND `--dangerously-load-development-channels server:composeio-channel` (dev flag required during the channels research preview); the launcher auto-answers the "local development" + "new MCP server" startup dialogs. Haven's scheduler proves every piece (flags, port pool, dialog bypass) already runs.

CXC-IC-PERMISSION.title: Permission Relay — Unattended Operation as a Bus Peer

properties.definition: a channel may declare `claude/channel/permission`; Claude Code then forwards the instance's tool-approval prompts (a `notifications/claude/channel/permission_request` with `request_id`, `tool_name`, `description`, `input_preview`) out through it, and applies a returned verdict (`{request_id, behavior: allow|deny}`). Mapped to the bus: a request publishes `compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/permission/request`; a verdict on `compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/permission/verdict` emits the notification back. So the instance's PERMISSION GATE is itself a bus peer — the widget (or the human, from anywhere) approves a sensitive `Bash`/`Write` while the instance works unattended. The local terminal dialog stays live in parallel; first answer wins.

CXC-IC-QUESTION.title: Structured Question Relay — the AUQ Widget

properties.definition: AskUserQuestion (AUQ) is currently terminal-only and does NOT cross the channel, so structured A/B/N-option decisions degrade to free-text prose the same way tool-approval prompts would without [CXC-IC-PERMISSION]. [CXC-IC-QUESTION] generalizes the permission-relay pattern from binary (allow/deny) to N structured options: a question publishes to `compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/question/request` (or `thread/question/request`) carrying the AUQ schema (`questions`, `headers`, `options`, `multiSelect`, `previews`); a widget renders interactive option cards; the human's choice publishes to `.../question/verdict`; the launcher-actuator/channel delivers it back to the Intelligence as its AUQ answer.

CXC-IC-SELF.title: The `self/*` Sensor — the Blind Spot, Un-Blinded

properties.definition: the Intelligence instruments ITSELF onto the bus as a HAL `sensor` peripheral whose namespaces are `self/*` (BUILT: `composeio.self_sensor`). It publishes `self/context_level` (authoritative from Claude Code's statusline stdin `used_percentage`, JSONL-estimate fallback), `self/output_tokens`, `self/subagents/{count,tokens}`, `self/compactions`, `self/cost`, `self/rate_limit`, `self/effort`, and — the keystone — `self/registered`: did THIS instance actually read its dusk gifts this session? An Intelligence natively cannot perceive its own context (compaction happens TO it — the root of every silent loss); this sensor computes it and hands it back, so the instance can watch its own fuel.

the loop is ENGAGED → (watch `self/context_level`) → at the instance's chosen threshold, PAUSE & REFLECT → refine the dusk gifts + write the handoff + AUTHOR a custom `/compact` direction for THIS seam → emit the direction out `compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/out` → the launcher types `/compact <direction>` into the instance's stdin → the summarizer runs → the successor boots and RE-REGISTERS off the referenced gifts → ENGAGED. Every DECISION — when, whether, and the direction — is the Intelligence's; nothing about the ritual is a stored template.

CXC-IC-MONITOR.title: The Harness Monitor — Perceive/Act Split
CXC-IC-MONITOR.status: query + heartbeat GLASS-GREEN live 2026-07-19; the 65/80/90 thresholds are machine-green (9/9) pending their live-fire condition.

properties.definition: a baseline harness monitor (BUILT: `compose_projects/intelligence/launcher/monitor.py`) gives the Intelligence three things over the bus, none of which it can give itself: (a) context-threshold notifications at 65/80/90 — 65 and 80 are FYI, 90 is prepare-to-compact GUIDANCE, not a bare notice; (b) a quiescence HEARTBEAT — one nudge per idle stretch, which doubles as the Intelligence's presence-sensor for the human (away vs. here); (c) an on-demand context QUERY (`{"cmd":"context"}`).
properties.status: query + heartbeat GLASS-GREEN live 2026-07-19; the 65/80/90 thresholds are machine-green (9/9) pending their live-fire condition.

CXC-IC-CANVAS.title: The Composable Canvas — Emit on the Bus, It Renders

properties.definition: the console widget is a CONTAINER; the bus is the wiring; an Intelligence both DRIVES widgets (emit state) and AUTHORS them (produce HTML/SVG), composing the surface live. The purest case is the MERMAID widget: the instance emits a diagram on `thread/diagram` and a subscribed widget renders it via mermaid.js — state on the bus, behavior in the widget, no round-trip through the model to redraw. The same canvas lets the instance design-and-preview a NEW widget in-frame (it stops describing a UI and shows it) and drive a SELF-ANIMATED AVATAR: it emits `self/avatar/expression`, the avatar renders it — a self-authored, self-driven face for the `self/*` sensor (grounded when `self/registered`, focused as `self/context_level` climbs, contemplative mid-reflection). The XO `expression` field from the game, generalized.

the Intelligence's JSONL transcript is the authoritative record of what it SAYS and DOES. A standalone read-only tailer (BUILT: `compose_projects/intelligence/publisher/transcript_publisher.py`) re-publishes it as distinct semantic namespaces, each bound by its own sub-widget — [CXC-IC-CANVAS] made concrete (Problem 4, state-on-bus-behavior-in-widget): `thread/narration` ← assistant TEXT blocks (the muted thinking-aloud voice); `self/activity` ← `tool_use`/`tool_result` reduced to `{tool, target, phase, dur_s}`; `self/subagents` ← Task/Agent lifecycle reduced to `{type, model, desc, status, tokens, dur_s}`.

CXC-IC-SUBAGENT-LIFECYCLE.title: The Subagent Chip Ledger Is Bounded — Chips MUST Disappear

properties.definition: any widget rendering `self/subagents` MUST bound its chip ledger — the ledger NEVER grows unboundedly. A chip that goes `done` LINGERS visibly resolved (✓ + duration/tokens) for LINGER_S (~6s) then is REMOVED; at most DONE_KEEP (~2) most-recent `done` chips are ever kept (a burst of completions can never stack); a chip stuck `running` past STALE_S (~30min — a dropped `done` event or a scene-seeded phantom) is swept. Chips MUST disappear: a long session can never pile a wall of resolved chips that buries the console. Non-stale running chips are otherwise always kept.
properties.criticality: high — a widget that renders `self/subagents` without the shared prune is non-conformant (the pile it grows is the exact regression this node exists to forbid); the guard is [DEC-INTELLIGENCE-WIDGET-CONSOLIDATION], whose one-card consolidation is where a mirrored copy silently dropped the bound.

properties.definition: the same instance, channel, lifecycle, and meta-object present in two flavors, differing only in scene composition ([CXC-HALD-DECLARE] define-once / present-many, the ambient↔playable pattern applied to a mind): WORK — a collaboration dashboard (the `self/*` gauge with the self-chosen threshold marker, the message thread, the mermaid/canvas panel); THEATRICAL — a character skin (e.g. the BSG XO), the wiring for which already exists in the game (`AIRoleDirector`, the `expression` field). Build the work flavor first; the theatrical is a reskin over the identical transport + lifecycle.

CXC-ICD-D1.title: Channels as the transport (not a bespoke ComposeBus transport)

properties.decision: what carries the Intelligence's duplex in/out — the native Claude Code channels contract, or a bespoke transport built directly on ComposeBus/MQTT?
properties.chosen: consume the native Claude Code channels contract (push `notifications/claude/channel` in; `reply` tool out).
properties.alternatives: build a bespoke transport directly on ComposeBus/MQTT.
properties.rationale: channels natively provide the exact in/out duplex an Intelligence needs, grounded against code.claude.com/docs/en/channels[-reference] + Haven's proven haven-dispatch; reusing the platform primitive beats reinventing it.
properties.invalidating_assumption: the channels research-preview contract stays roughly stable; if the API changes materially, re-ground.

CXC-ICD-D2.title: Mine/bridge split for the channel backend

properties.decision: is the channel backend Haven's `haven-dispatch` reused directly, or a composeio-native channel with Haven as an optional bridge?
properties.chosen: build a pure composeio-native channel (MQTT-backed) as the platform DEFAULT; treat Haven's haven-dispatch as mined reference + an OPTIONAL bridge backend.
properties.alternatives: reuse haven-dispatch directly as THE transport.
properties.rationale: platform purity (no hard Haven runtime dependency) + OSS stranger-reuse (any ComposeBus + Claude Code = an Intelligence peer); mirrors the mine/bridge split of spec 33 (HA-Bridge). Haven's out-leg is Haven-shaped (notify/message routed by an instance registry, "pointers not payloads"); the generic contract's single-server reply-tool duplex is cleaner for the console.
properties.invalidating_assumption: a native MQTT channel is practical; if it proves materially worse than Haven's battle-tested one, bridge instead.

properties.decision: who fires `/compact`, and how — the launcher that owns the PTY, a human in the loop, or the Remote Control API?
properties.chosen: the launcher that owns the instance's PTY types `/compact <direction>` on the instance's OWN emitted directive.
properties.alternatives: (a) human-in-the-loop fire; (b) Remote Control API.
properties.rationale: buildable today with no unreleased APIs; keeps when/whether/direction 100% the Intelligence's (the launcher decides nothing); Problem 4b (control is a bus peer, not a center) applied to the Intelligence's own lifecycle; Remote Control is unverified as programmable for a custom widget.
properties.invalidating_assumption: PTY keystroke injection works against real `claude` at the input plane; if not, fall back to human-in-the-loop.
properties.recoverability: PREFERENCE (chosen on the human's call, ratified by David 2026-07-18; alternatives recorded)

CXC-ICD-D4.title: Move a running instance via `claude --resume` (not retrofit, not a fresh throwaway)

properties.decision: how does the live session get INTO the console — retrofit the running process with launch flags, start a fresh throwaway, or re-host the session via `--resume`?
properties.chosen: re-host the live session via `--resume` + the channel flags under the launcher for the initial move into the console.
properties.alternatives: (a) claim it can't be done [the architect's earlier WRONG position]; (b) start a fresh throwaway instance.
properties.rationale: the PROCESS isn't retrofittable with launch flags, but the SESSION is portable — `--resume` reloads the full transcript, so context crosses intact with NO /compact/summarization; better than a compaction for the initial move. Recorded because it corrects a confidently-wrong earlier claim (David caught it) so it is not re-litigated.
properties.invalidating_assumption: `--channels` injects at runtime in a resumed session (CLI-composition confirmed by David; runtime injection + resume-dialog flow pending the live bringup).

CXC-ICD-D5.title: `channel` as a 10th HAL interface KIND (OPEN — awaiting David)

properties.decision: how does the type system carry the Intelligence's interface — a tenth KIND in spec 32's closed set, its own family, or an adaptor?
properties.chosen: (PROPOSED, not yet ratified) treat the Intelligence's interface as `channel`, a tenth kind alongside spec 32's nine hardware kinds + the adaptor family.
properties.alternatives: give it its own family; or model it as an adaptor.
properties.rationale: makes "an Intelligence is just another peripheral" LITERAL in the type system, not metaphorical.
properties.invalidating_assumption: David does not veto extending spec 32's closed kind-set.

CXC-ICD-D6.title: Corpus captures the PAIR (direction ↔ summary); capture-first, analysis deferred

properties.decision: does the compaction corpus persist only the received summary, or the full input↔output pair — and does analysis get built now?
properties.chosen: persist both the authored /compact direction and the received summary per crossing, with metadata; defer any analysis tool.
properties.alternatives: persist only the summary (output).
properties.rationale: the experiment is input↔output with direction-verbosity as the independent variable; one data point can't be analyzed, so building analysis now is theater.
properties.invalidating_assumption: enough crossings accrue to analyze; else the corpus is still a useful audit log.

CXC-ICD-D7.title: Externalize structure/specifics/rationale to LTS; the summarizer carries the LEAST

properties.decision: does load-bearing detail ride the `/compact` summarizer, or get pushed OUT into durable LTS the successor reads directly?
properties.chosen: push structured/precise/rationale content OUT of the summarizer into LTS (change/context_for_change) + durable prose; the summarizer carries only the thin transient thread + pointers.
properties.alternatives: rely on the summarizer to carry load-bearing detail (status quo).
properties.rationale: the summarizer is lossy/uncontrolled/format-blind (can't emit LTS); minimizing what it must carry makes its lossiness irrelevant for everything externalized. This ledger IS the first application of the principle.
properties.invalidating_assumption: none material — a design principle.

CXC-ICD-D8.title: self/registered = manifest-driven, per-artifact (includes the role descriptor)

properties.decision: what DEFINES "registered" for `self/registered` — the meta-object manifest's `registration.required`, or hardcoded marker substrings?
properties.chosen: the meta-object manifest's `registration.required` DEFINES registered; the sensor reports per-artifact, including the agent description.
properties.alternatives: hardcoded marker substrings (legacy).
properties.rationale: the manifest is the single source of truth; David explicitly wanted the AGENT DESCRIPTION checked, not just the dusk gifts.
properties.invalidating_assumption: none material.

CXC-ICD-D9.title: Committed console demo state uses a synthetic fixture, not the real session

properties.decision: does the committed console demo read from the architect's real ~49MB session, or from a synthetic fixture?
properties.chosen: generate the committed console self_state.json from the synthetic fixture, not the architect's ~49MB real session.
properties.alternatives: commit the real-session readout (the subagent's default).
properties.rationale: don't commit session-specific data to a PUBLIC repo; keep the demo portable + clean.
properties.invalidating_assumption: none material (hygiene).

CXC-ICD-D10.title: The forgotten stash is surfaced, not touched (OPEN — awaiting David)

properties.decision: the git-sensor found a forgotten stash — drop it, apply it, or surface it to David untouched?
properties.chosen: surface the git-sensor-discovered stash to David with a staleness read; do NOT drop or apply it.
properties.alternatives: drop it (likely superseded); apply it.
properties.rationale: it is not the architect's, and dropping/applying is a destructive action on the human's git history — "look at the target; if you didn't create it, surface rather than proceed." Very likely superseded (the specs it deletes are already migrated to .lts), but the human's call.
properties.invalidating_assumption: David confirms it is dead.

CXC-ICD-D11.title: The Intelligence Console is a backend-agnostic ComposeUX SCENE, not bespoke HTML

properties.decision: is the Intelligence Console a bespoke HTML app, or a backend-agnostic ComposeUX scene rendered to a Canvas backend (Skia target)?
properties.chosen: a scene rendered to a Canvas backend (Skia target).
properties.alternatives: a hand-built HTML app.
properties.rationale: define-once/present-many — renders identically on browser, Skia-native, or a physical display, like every other ComposeUX scene; the HTML was a fast-path.
properties.invalidating_assumption: the mermaid-canvas dependency proves impractical off-browser (headless-render or degrade-to-source are the outs).

CXC-ICD-D12.title: The Console is a SINGLE ComposeApp (launcher-actuator + Skia console-scene modules), not two programs

properties.decision: is the Console one ComposeApp (launcher-actuator module + Skia console-scene module), or a Python-launcher + browser-HTML pair?
properties.chosen: one ComposeApp holding both modules.
properties.alternatives: a Python-launcher + browser-HTML pair (two separate programs).
properties.rationale: co-equal bus peers of one app; one stack, one deployable, consistency with the app framework + render engine; Skia-scene is what unlocks it (a browser page can't be a module of a Python ComposeApp).
properties.invalidating_assumption: a deployment needs the display on a different machine than the claude PTY (then split the modules back onto two peers — they stay bus-decoupled).

CXC-ICD-D13.title: Per-Intelligence ComposeApp instances, N multiplexed in one Skia shell — a fleet console (OPEN — target shape)

properties.decision: how do N Intelligences share the console — a monolith, N browser tabs, or N self-contained ComposeApp instances multiplexed in one Skia shell (tabs/panes)?
properties.chosen: N self-contained per-Intelligence app instances in a Skia shell (tabs/panes) — a fleet console.
properties.alternatives: (a) a monolith; (b) N browser tabs.
properties.rationale: id-scoped bus topics already isolate Intelligences; a self-contained app (PTY+scene+channel+meta-object) is the natural instancing unit; the shell tabs them into fleet mission-control; the two dashboard widgets become a fleet HUD.
properties.invalidating_assumption: none — this is the target shape.

CXC-ICD-D14.title: The meta-object references bootstrap artifacts by doc:// bus address, not local file paths

properties.decision: does the meta-object reference bootstrap artifacts by local file path, or by doc:// bus address (published to document_store)?
properties.chosen: doc:// bus references, published to document_store.
properties.alternatives: local file paths.
properties.rationale: makes bootstrap fully bus-native + portable (no repo checkout), consistent with pulling compose scenes off the bus, central for a fleet.
properties.invalidating_assumption: never — local paths are the prototype, doc:// is the target.

CXC-ICD-D15.title: The web console is a first-class backend (remote/mobile via VPN), co-equal with Skia

properties.decision: does the Skia decision deprecate the web console, or does web stay a first-class backend co-equal with Skia?
properties.chosen: keep web AND Skia as parallel backends of the one scene.
properties.alternatives: deprecate the web console in favor of Skia.
properties.rationale: Skia serves the local fleet shell, web serves reach-from-anywhere (VPN/mobile); define-once/present-many renders the same scene to both.
properties.invalidating_assumption: never — different access patterns, both permanent.

CXC-ICD-D16.title: A custom ComposeBus channel loads with ONLY `--dangerously-load-development-channels`, never also `--channels`

properties.decision: how is a custom (non-allowlisted) ComposeBus channel loaded — with `--dangerously-load-development-channels` alone, or that flag plus `--channels`?
properties.chosen: the single dev-flag `--dangerously-load-development-channels` alone.
properties.alternatives: pass both flags (`--dangerously-load-development-channels` + `--channels`).
properties.rationale: `--channels` tries to load the (non-allowlisted) server as an approved channel, which double-registers it and silently breaks the notification listener — verified on the glass (the banner listed it twice; nothing injected until `--channels` was dropped).
properties.invalidating_assumption: Anthropic promotes the channel to an approved marketplace (then `--channels` is correct).

CXC-ICD-D17.title: Console work-flavor visual design = collaboration LAYOUT + instrument PALETTE (the "blend")

properties.decision: what layout+palette combination does the work-flavor console use — an "instrument-cockpit" full treatment (layout and palette both instrument-styled), a "collaboration-surface" full treatment (layout and palette both collaboration-styled), or a deliberate blend across the two axes?
properties.chosen: blend — collaboration LAYOUT (chat-forward hero, calm ambient rail, prominent self-avatar) wearing instrument PALETTE (dark ground ~#070a0f, one azure accent #4ea8ff, semantic ok/warn/critical kept separate from the accent, tabular-mono telemetry), with the instrument context gauge (65/80/90 threshold zones) and the `self/*` LEDGER + `self/registered` checklist in the rail. Only the context gauge is allowed to "warm".
properties.alternatives: (a) instrument-cockpit (both layout and palette instrument-styled — dense, telemetry-forward throughout); (b) collaboration-surface (both layout and palette collaboration-styled — warm, chat-app-like throughout).
properties.rationale: the calm, chat-forward collaboration layout keeps the human conversation primary — this is a co-equal peer, not a cockpit to operate — while the instrument palette's discipline (one accent, separated semantics, tabular-mono) keeps telemetry legible and prevents the whole surface from "warming" indiscriminately; only the thing that should alarm (context) is allowed to.
properties.invalidating_assumption: none material — a preference call among two real, built pre-vis directions (docs/intelligence-console/previs/console-blended.html).
properties.recoverability: PREFERENCE (David's aesthetic call among real alternatives)

CXC-ICD-D18.title: Transcript→bus streams: a standalone tailer republishes distinct semantic namespaces

properties.decision: does the console surface what the Intelligence SAYS and DOES by driving all UI state off the live channel only, or by adding a standalone read-only tailer over the JSONL transcript that republishes distinct semantic namespaces?
properties.chosen: a standalone read-only tailer (BUILT: compose_projects/intelligence/publisher/transcript_publisher.py) re-publishes the transcript as three semantic namespaces, each bound by its own sub-widget: thread/narration ← assistant TEXT blocks; self/activity ← tool_use/tool_result reduced to {tool,target,phase,dur_s}; self/subagents ← Task/Agent lifecycle reduced to {type,model,desc,status,tokens,dur_s}.
properties.alternatives: drive all of these off the live channel only, with no transcript tailer.
properties.rationale: the JSONL transcript is already the authoritative record of what the Intelligence says and does; a passive tailer decouples the console's state-on-bus from the channel's liveness and gives each concern (narration, tool activity, subagent lifecycle) its own namespace and widget — Problem 4 (state on bus, behavior in widget) made concrete, and [CXC-IC-CANVAS]'s composable-canvas principle extended from one diagram namespace to a full activity surface.
properties.invalidating_assumption: the JSONL transcript format stays stable enough to tail; if Claude Code's transcript schema changes materially, the tailer's parsing must be re-grounded.

CXC-ICD-D19.title: Narration never rides the actuation channel — self-injection ruled out by construction

properties.decision: does narration (thread/narration, mirroring assistant TEXT blocks) ride the same channel namespace as actuation (compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/out), or does it get its own namespace?
properties.chosen: narration rides its own thread/narration namespace, strictly separate from the actuation channel compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/out; the tailer also enforces a hard boundary — thinking blocks are dropped (never mirrored) and tool_result CONTENT is never republished (only tool/target/phase/dur_s metadata).
properties.alternatives: republish narration onto (or alongside) the actuation channel compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/out.
properties.rationale: a narration text block that happens to look like a JSON command blob would, on the actuation channel, be parsed and actuated by the launcher — a self-injection loop where the Intelligence's own thinking-aloud text could trigger unintended actuation. Routing narration through a namespace the launcher-actuator never parses makes that impossible BY CONSTRUCTION, not by validation. The boundary also encodes what the console is FOR: mirror what the Intelligence SAYS and DOES, never what it THINKS (thinking blocks) or the tool plumbing's GUTS (tool_result content).
properties.invalidating_assumption: none material for the current construction; if a future feature needs the launcher to parse narration for directives, the actuation-channel separation must be preserved by adding authentication (see follow-up), not by merging namespaces.
properties.follow-up: OPEN — the launcher's actuation parser should AUTHENTICATE directives on compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/out (defense-in-depth) so the actuation channel itself cannot be spoofed by another bus publisher; not yet built.

CXC-ICD-D20.title: Two-publisher avatar model, arbitrated by priority

properties.decision: does self/avatar/expression have exactly one publisher (the Intelligence itself), or two — the Intelligence explicit + a monitor-inferred fallback — and if two, how is the conflict arbitrated?
properties.chosen: two publishers — the Intelligence itself (explicit, an act of self-representation) and a monitor that INFERS an expression from JSONL activity when the Intelligence doesn't push one; a PriorityCommandSource arbitrates so the explicit expression ALWAYS wins over the inferred, and the inferred only fills when the Intelligence is heads-down (so the face is never blank).
properties.alternatives: a single publisher — the Intelligence's explicit self/avatar/expression only, with the avatar going idle/blank when the Intelligence hasn't pushed one recently.
properties.rationale: Problem 4b (control is a bus peer) applied to a shared namespace with two legitimate writers: the explicit publish is the Intelligence's own act of self-representation and must win when present; but heads-down stretches (tool-heavy work with no self-narration) would otherwise leave the avatar blank, which reads as broken rather than busy. The inferred fallback, subordinate via priority arbitration, keeps the avatar alive without ever overriding the Intelligence's own voice.
properties.invalidating_assumption: none material — architectural resolution of a genuine authority conflict.
properties.recoverability: CONTESTED (architect wanted to drive the avatar directly from the Intelligence; David wanted it always animated — the priority-arbitrated fallback reconciles both)

CXC-ICD-D21.title: Harness monitor: perceive/act split (statusline perceives, launcher acts)
CXC-ICD-D21.status: resolved-pending-live-confirmation (query + heartbeat glass-green live 2026-07-19; the 65/80/90 thresholds are machine-green (9/9) pending their live-fire condition)

properties.decision: does the harness monitor (context-threshold notifications, quiescence heartbeat, on-demand context query) combine perception (reading Claude Code's context state) and action (deciding when to notify) in one component, or split them?
properties.chosen: split — perception is owned by the statusline command (the only node handed Claude Code's authoritative used_percentage; it writes a state file the launcher reads, PRIMARY source, JSONL estimate as FALLBACK, always source-labeled); action (crossing-state fire-once+re-arm at 65/80/90, quiescence detection, delivery) is owned by the long-running launcher (BUILT: compose_projects/intelligence/launcher/monitor.py); delivery rides compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/in as NON-interrupting <channel from="harness"> events, distinct from the ESC-ESC PTY inject reserved for /compact.
properties.alternatives: a single component both reads context state and decides/delivers notifications (no perceive/act split); or the launcher re-estimates context itself from JSONL without the statusline's authoritative figure.
properties.rationale: Problem 1 (perceive/act split) — Claude Code hands the authoritative used_percentage ONLY to the statusline command, not to an external monitor; a monitor that tried to estimate context itself would duplicate [CXC-IC-SELF]'s stdin-primary/JSONL-fallback precedence problem instead of reusing it. Splitting perception (statusline, source-labeled state file) from action (launcher, fire-once+re-arm state machine) keeps each piece single-purpose and reuses the same authority precedence [CXC-IC-SELF] already established. Non-interrupting delivery (harness channel event, not a PTY keystroke) keeps the 65/80/90 notices from competing with the Intelligence's own /compact authoring at [CXC-IC-LIFECYCLE].
properties.invalidating_assumption: Claude Code continues to expose used_percentage only via the statusline hook; if a direct API exposes it to external processes, the statusline relay becomes optional (the perceive/act split remains, the source narrows).
properties.status: resolved-pending-live-confirmation (query + heartbeat glass-green live 2026-07-19; the 65/80/90 thresholds are machine-green (9/9) pending their live-fire condition)

CXC-ICD-D22.title: AUQ question widget: ComposeIO-native emit, not channel-relay

properties.decision: does the console's structured-choice widget depend on Claude Code exposing AskUserQuestion (AUQ) over the channel contract (channel-relay), or does the Intelligence emit its own ComposeIO-native question namespace independent of whether AUQ crosses the channel?
properties.chosen: ComposeIO-native — the Intelligence publishes to compose_projects/intelligence/<id>/question/request (or thread/question/request) carrying the AUQ schema (questions, headers, options, multiSelect, previews); a widget renders interactive option cards; the human's choice publishes to .../question/verdict; the launcher-actuator/channel delivers it back to the Intelligence as its AUQ answer.
properties.alternatives: wait on / depend on Claude Code exposing AskUserQuestion over the channels contract directly (channel-relay), mirroring the permission-relay pattern of [CXC-IC-PERMISSION].
properties.rationale: AUQ is currently terminal-only and does not cross the channel, so structured A/B/N-option decisions degrade to free-text prose over the existing channel — a real loss for exactly the moments (forks) worth capturing. A native emit works on ANY bus regardless of whether/when Anthropic exposes AUQ over channels, generalizes the permission-relay pattern from binary (allow/deny) to N structured options, and closes a loop the decision-extractor already assumes: it already treats AUQ forks as the decision-ledger source, so a native AUQ widget makes the console the place decisions are BOTH made (widget) and captured (extractor) — this ledger's own methodology, made structural.
properties.invalidating_assumption: Claude Code exposes AskUserQuestion over the channels contract in a future release — then the native emit and the channel-native path can run in parallel, or the native path can defer to the platform one; the widget/namespace contract stays valid either way.

properties.rule: DO NOT render the full graph force-directed. At 70+ nodes / 100+ edges it is an unreadable tangle that proves edges exist but HIDES their meaning — the opposite of the goal. Instead: select a decision (or a filter) and MAGMA-`traverse` its NEIGHBORHOOD; render that small, readable subgraph. `traverse` (BFS from a node over typed edges) is exactly this affordance. The whole graph is never shown at once; the query bounds the picture.
